title: WNBA will not rescind Caitlin Clark’s technical foul from Fever-Mercury game
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — The WNBA did not rescind the technical foul Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark received in Monday’s win over the Phoenix Mercury, the league told The Athletic on Wednesday. Clark’s technical foul will stand, which keeps her at five technical fouls on the season. If players reach eight technical fouls, they are automatically suspended for one game, per league rules.

“We should all just go on the calendar now and pick a game that I’m gonna be suspended for if I’m gonna get technicals for clapping,” Clark said.

Clark was assessed a technical foul in the fourth quarter of Monday’s game after a dust-up with Phoenix Mercury forward DeWanna Bonner, who was formerly Clark’s teammate on the Fever. Clark fouled Bonner, and the two appeared to take exception to the contact and they exchanged words. While the officials tried to diffuse the situation, Clark began clapping toward Phoenix players, an act the officials deemed as “instigating,” according to Clark.

This story will be updated.
